item.description:
## Added

- Speecher now runs on Windows. The installer sets up a native app with the
  same dictation pill, tray icon, settings window and update channels as the
  other platforms; delivery types into whatever window is focused, and the
  pill grows with the preview text as you speak.
- Speecher checks for updates every 30 minutes. A new Check frequency setting
  under Updates changes the schedule (up to once a day), and the check timer
  backs off politely when the network is down.
- When an update is waiting, a banner appears above the dictation popup with
  an Install and restart button. One click downloads the update in the
  background, installs it, and restarts Speecher — and if you were mid
  dictation, the restart waits until you finish and then puts you right back
  where you were, microphone open. The settings window's update banner is the
  same single click now.
- After an update, a banner above the popup offers See what's new and opens
  the release notes. It slips away after a few seconds and returns with the
  next dictation until you follow it or dismiss it.
- The setup assistant on macOS is a native window, matching the rest of the
  mac app.
- Setting up a provider now shows its live status, and the popup streams the
  refined text into the preview as it arrives instead of waiting for the
  whole result.

## Changed

- Once a dictation is delivered, the popup shows just the outcome — the icon
  and what happened — instead of the waveform and transcript machinery.
- Updates on macOS are driven by Speecher's own banners and buttons rather
  than Sparkle's dialog boxes. Checking, downloading, and restarting look the
  same on every platform now, and a manual Check now always answers, even
  when the news is "you're up to date" or the check failed.

## Fixed

- macOS: the microphone permission prompt no longer cancels the first
  dictation, Claude sign-in reads and refreshes the native login from the
  Keychain, and copying something new while Speecher restores the clipboard
  no longer loses your copy (also fixed on Windows).
- A speech stream that drops mid-sentence reconnects and carries on instead
  of delivering half a sentence.
- Starting a new dictation no longer flashes the previous dictation's words
  in the popup.

## Requirements

- Windows: 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1809) or later.
